question: How much is the yearly deductible for just me on the Standard Option?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: $350 per person calendar-year deductible under Standard Option ($700 combined for Self and Family). Section 4 (PDF p.30) and Standard Option summary (PDF p.164).

question: How long is the window when I can first sign up for Medicare Part B around my 65th birthday?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: A 7-month Initial Enrollment Period: 3 months before the month you turn 65, the birthday month, and 3 months after. PDF p.17.

question: On Standard Option, what's my copay to see a specialist who is in the PPO network?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: $40 copayment per visit for a Preferred specialist, no deductible. Section 5(a) table (PDF p.41) and summary (PDF p.164).

question: I'm in the hospital for 75 days straight under Original Medicare. How much do I owe per day for the days after the first 60?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Days 61-90 of a benefit period cost $434 per day (2026 amount). PDF p.30.

question: I got rushed to the hospital last night and was admitted. Do I have to call my FEP plan about it, and by when?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: You, your representative, the physician or the hospital must phone the Plan within two business days after an emergency admission, even if you have been discharged. PDF p.28.

question: I'm a federal retiree with an OPM annuity and I don't get Social Security. How do I get my Part B premium paid?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Ask to have the Part B premium deducted from your OPM annuity by contacting your local Social Security office; otherwise you get a bill. PDF p.24.

question: What will the Standard Option calendar year deductible be in 2027?
reference: Not answerable. The brochure covers 2026 only ($350) and gives no 2027 amount.

question: I'm thinking about Basic Option, Self Only. Is there a deductible I have to meet first, and what's the most I could pay out of pocket in a year if I stick with PPO providers?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Basic Option has no calendar-year deductible (PDF p.30, 41, 166); Self Only catastrophic out-of-pocket maximum is $7,500 for PPO providers (PDF p.35, 167).

question: If I went 29 months without any drug coverage before joining a Part D plan, roughly how much would my monthly late penalty be in 2026?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: The penalty is 1% per uncovered month (29%) of the national base beneficiary premium ($38.99 in 2026), about $11.31, rounded to $11.30 per month. PDF p.88 (method, base premium) and p.89 (2026 example).

question: How long do I have to be in the hospital before Medicare will pay for a stay in a nursing home?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: A prior medically necessary inpatient hospital stay of 3 days in a row or more (not counting the day of discharge) for skilled nursing facility coverage; some ACO waivers may remove this. PDF p.31-32.

question: What's the most I'd pay out of pocket in a year on Standard Option if I'm single and only use PPO providers?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Standard Option Self Only catastrophic protection out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 for Preferred providers ($8,000 PPO and non-PPO combined). PDF p.35 and p.165.

question: I need an MRI done in a hospital's outpatient department. What will the hospital charge me on Basic Option?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Basic Option Preferred facility: $250 copayment per day per facility for outpatient CT/MRI/PET billed by a facility. PDF p.81 (table checked on the page image) and summary p.166.

question: My mom is in a skilled nursing facility and it's day 45 of her stay. What does Medicare charge her per day?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Days 21-100 in a skilled nursing facility cost $217 per day (2026 amount). PDF p.31.

question: What's the standard monthly Part B premium for 2027?
reference: Not answerable. The 2027 premium amounts were not available at printing (PDF p.12); only the 2026 amount ($202.90, p.23) is given.

question: My claim was denied and I want the plan to take another look. How long do I have to ask, and where do I send the request?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Write to the Plan within 6 months of its decision, at the address on your explanation of benefits (EOB), with your reasons and supporting documents. Section 8, PDF p.140.

question: I'm 67, still working with my employer's insurance, and I skipped Part B. When can I sign up without a penalty?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Special Enrollment Period: any time you're still covered by the group health plan, or during the 8-month period that begins the month after the employment or coverage ends. PDF p.17.

question: What enrollment code do I use to sign up for Basic Option Self Plus One?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Enrollment code 113 (Basic Option Self Plus One). Cover page (PDF p.1) and rate table (PDF p.168).

question: What happens to my Part B premium if I put off signing up when I first became eligible?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: The monthly premium may go up 10% for each full 12 months you could have had Part B but didn't sign up, for as long as you have Part B. PDF p.23.

question: What's the biweekly premium for Aetna's FEHB plan for Self Only?
reference: Not answerable. The brochure only lists rates for the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan (PDF p.168).

question: If I'm admitted to the hospital on Basic Option, what do I pay and is there a cap on it?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Preferred facility: $425 copayment per day, up to $2,975 per admission. PDF p.77, summary p.166, and 2026 changes p.17.

question: Which Medigap plans cover Part B excess charges?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Only Medigap Plans F and G pay (100%) Part B excess charges. PDF p.80 (table read from the page image because the extracted text is jumbled).

question: I have Basic Option and Medicare Part B is my primary coverage. What's the most I pay for a preferred brand-name drug at a retail pharmacy for 30 days, and through the mail-order program?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Retail Tier 2: 35% of the Plan allowance, $100 maximum with Part B primary (PDF p.166, 105, 18); mail service preferred brand: 35% up to a $225 maximum (PDF p.167, 106, 18).

question: When can I switch my Medicare drug plan for next year, and what's the cap on my yearly drug costs?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Open Enrollment Period October 15 - December 7 each year (PDF p.84, 13); out-of-pocket drug costs are capped at $2,400 in 2027 (PDF p.85, 87).

question: What's the income limit for the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary program in Texas?
reference: Not answerable. Medicare Savings Program limits vary by state and the book gives no state figures (PDF p.96).

question: What do I get for filling out the Blue Health Assessment?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: A $50 health account for most health-related expenses (up to $170 total with goals). Section 5(h), PDF p.127.

question: My doctor says she has 'opted out' of Medicare. For how long does that last?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: A provider must opt out for 2 years, and it renews automatically every 2 years unless they ask not to renew. PDF p.64.

question: How do I place my first mail-order prescription, and how long should I expect it to take?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Complete the initial mail order form, enclose the prescription and copayment, mail it to CVS Caremark, and allow up to two weeks (refills up to ten days). PDF p.138.

question: I lost my Medicare card. How do I get a new one?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Log into your secure Medicare account at Medicare.gov to print or order a replacement, or call 1-800-MEDICARE (RRB beneficiaries can call the RRB). PDF p.27.

question: I'm on Standard Option and need a ground ambulance for a medical emergency. What do I pay?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: $100 copayment per day for ground ambulance (no deductible); $150 per day for air or sea. PDF p.88 and summary p.164.

question: What's the out-of-pocket limit for Medigap Plan K in 2026?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: $8,000 for Plan K ($4,000 for Plan L) in 2026. PDF p.80.

question: How much will my Ozempic prescription cost me on Standard Option?
reference: Not answerable. The brochure gives cost-shares per drug tier but does not list individual drugs or their tier.

question: Under the plan's Medicare prescription drug program, what's the most I'd pay out of pocket for covered drugs in a year?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: The separate FEP Medicare Prescription Drug Program catastrophic maximum is $2,100 under both Standard and Basic Option. PDF p.112 and 2026 changes p.19.

question: If a doctor doesn't accept assignment, what's the most extra they can charge me above the Medicare-approved amount?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: In many cases no more than 15% above the Medicare-approved amount (the limiting charge). PDF p.64.

question: I'm on Basic Option. What will a routine dental cleaning and exam cost me with a PPO dentist?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: $35 copayment per evaluation (exam, cleaning and X-rays), most services limited to 2 per year. PDF p.125 and summary p.167.

question: Which Medigap plans help pay for emergency care while I'm traveling abroad, and how much do they pay?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Plans C, D, F, G, M and N pay 80% of foreign travel emergency care, up to plan limits. PDF p.80 (read from the page image).

question: What's the typical monthly premium for a Medigap Plan G policy in Florida?
reference: Not answerable. The book describes Medigap plans but gives no premium amounts or state prices.

question: My surgeon wants to do an elective knee replacement as an outpatient. Do I need to do anything with the plan before the surgery?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Yes. Prior approval is required for elective non-urgent hip, knee and spine surgery in any setting; call the customer service number on the back of your ID card before the surgery. PDF p.25 (also p.19, 64, 76).

question: How do I appeal a decision about a claim under Original Medicare?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Take the Medicare Summary Notice showing the item, circle it, explain why you disagree, and send it to the Medicare Administrative Contractor listed on it (or use Form CMS-20027) by the date on the MSN. PDF p.103.

question: I work for the Postal Service. Can I enroll in the Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan for 2026?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: No. Postal Employees and Annuitants are no longer eligible for this Plan (unless currently under Temporary Continuation of Coverage). Cover page, PDF p.1.

question: Is there a cap on what I pay per month for insulin?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Insulin covered under Part B (pump) or Part D plans can't cost more than $35 for a one-month supply. PDF p.41 and p.92.

question: I have Basic Option and I'm taken by ground ambulance to a Preferred hospital's emergency room. What will the ambulance and the ER cost me?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Ground ambulance: $250 copayment per day (PDF p.88, 19); emergency room: $425 copayment per day per facility (PDF p.91-92, 18). Both on summary p.166.

question: What's the yearly Part B deductible in 2026, and which Medigap plans pay it?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: $283 in 2026 (PDF p.32, 80). Medigap Plans C and F pay 100% of the Part B deductible (K and L after their out-of-pocket limit). PDF p.80, read from the page image.

question: How much is my share of the biweekly premium for Standard Option Self Only?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: $188.32 biweekly (enrollee share; $408.02 monthly) for code 104. Rate table, PDF p.168.

question: If I'm single, what yearly income do I have to be under to qualify for Extra Help in 2026?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: Less than $23,940 a year for a single person (resources under $18,090); higher limits in some situations. PDF p.96.

question: Is Dr. Sarah Chen at Mercy General Hospital a Preferred provider under Basic Option?
reference: Not answerable. The brochure does not list individual providers; it points members to the online provider finder.

question: I'm retired and covered by this FEHB plan. Do I need to sign up for Medicare Part D, or will I get hit with a late penalty later?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: No. The Plan's drug coverage is creditable, so you don't need Part D and won't pay a late-enrollment penalty as long as you keep FEHB coverage. PDF p.2.

question: What's the most a Part D plan's deductible can be in 2027?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: No more than $700 in 2027. PDF p.86.

question: On Basic Option, will the plan pay anything if I see a doctor who isn't a Preferred provider?
document: 2026 FEHB Blue Cross Blue Shield Service Benefit Plan Brochure (RI 71-005)
reference: Generally no. Basic Option provides no benefits for Participating/Non-participating providers (you pay all charges), except in the exceptions listed in Section 3. PDF p.32, 41, 166.

question: How much is the hospital deductible I pay under Original Medicare each time I start a new benefit period?
document: Medicare & You 2027
reference: $1,736 in 2026 for each benefit period. PDF p.30 (also p.31 for skilled nursing facility care).

question: Does the Humana Gold Plus HMO plan cover dental implants?
reference: Not answerable. The book describes plan types in general and names no specific Medicare Advantage plans or their benefits.
